body_html:
Love, Slowly, or Amor, despacio in Spanish, is my second bilingual book, and probably the most personal one to write. It collects 300 small truths about crushes, first dates, situationships, heartbreak, friendship, family and the hardest love of all: learning to choose yourself. Like my other books, it is written in English with real Spanish woven into every page, plus a Spanish Note on how the language works. I wanted learning Spanish to feel less like homework and more like reading letters from a friend who understands your heart. Here is why I wrote it, what is inside and how I hope you will read it.

The book at a glance
  • Title: Love, Slowly | Amor, despacio
  • What it is: 300 bilingual truths about love, heartbreak and choosing yourself
  • Special pages: “To the one who…” letters and “Love Note” pages worth sharing
  • Spanish: a Spanish Note on every page, from te quiero vs te amo to false friends
  • Length: 304 pages, published in November 2026, readable in any order
{{toc}}

Why I wrote Love, Slowly

Love is the reason many people start learning Spanish. A partner from Guadalajara, a crush who speaks it at home, a family you are about to become part of. And yet most Spanish materials treat love as a vocabulary topic: a list of pet names and a few phrases for Valentine’s Day. Real love is messier than that. It is the text you don’t know how to answer, the apology you can’t find words for, the goodbye that takes months to understand.

As a translator, I have seen how differently the two languages handle these moments. Spanish has two ways to say “I love you”, and choosing the wrong one can make a first “I love you” sound like a marriage proposal. It has me haces falta, a way of saying “I miss you” that really means “something is missing without you”. These are not grammar points. They are emotional choices, and I wanted a book that treats them that way.

So I wrote the book I would want to read after a hard week: short pages about love as it really is, with the Spanish you need for exactly those feelings.

What you will find inside

Love, Slowly follows love through all its stages, not just the happy ones:

  • Crushes and first dates: the nervous, hopeful beginning.
  • Situationships: the in-between relationships that never quite get a name.
  • Heartbreak: what it feels like, and what it slowly teaches you.
  • Friendship and family: the loves that hold us up when romance doesn’t.
  • Choosing yourself: self-respect, boundaries and the patience to wait for the right kind of love.

The title is the advice I most needed to hear myself. Love that grows slowly, with care and honesty, tends to last. So does a language.

{{image:2}}

Letters, Love Notes and Spanish Notes

Most pages are a short truth, but a few special formats run through the book:

  • “To the one who…” letters, written to the people we have loved, lost or are still waiting for. Many readers will recognize someone in them.
  • “Love Note” pages, short lines meant to be shared: sent to a friend, posted, or kept for a bad day.
  • A Spanish Note on every page, explaining one thing about the language behind the feeling: te quiero vs te amo, a false friend that could cause an awkward moment, or how people really say something in conversation.

The difference between te quiero and te amo is a good example of the kind of thing I explain. Te quiero is warm and used with partners, family and close friends; te amo is deeper and saved for romantic love or very profound bonds. I wrote a full guide to {{link:te-quiero-vs-te-amo|te quiero vs te amo}} on this site, and the book returns to the idea in many small ways.

Why a love book is a good way to learn Spanish

We remember what we feel. A phrase you read on a page that describes your own heartbreak, or your own hope, sticks in a way a vocabulary list never will. That emotional connection is the whole point of the book.

It also teaches a kind of Spanish that textbooks rarely cover: how to say “I’m sorry” and mean it, how to reassure someone, how to set a boundary kindly, how to tell someone they matter. If you want to use that Spanish in real life, my guides to {{link:how-to-say-i-miss-you-in-spanish|saying I miss you in Spanish}}, {{link:apologizing-to-your-partner-in-spanish|apologizing to your partner}} and {{link:spanish-terms-of-endearment|Spanish terms of endearment}} go deeper into specific moments.

{{book:love-slowly}}

Who this book is for

  • People in a relationship with a Spanish speaker who want words for real feelings, not just greetings.
  • Learners with some Spanish who want something more personal than a textbook.
  • Anyone going through a breakup or a confusing relationship who would like company in short, gentle pages.
  • Readers who love to share quotes with friends, partners or followers.

Like my other books, it is a reading companion rather than a course. If you are a complete beginner, it works best alongside some basic study.

How I suggest reading it

Love, Slowly is designed to be read in any order, one page a day. Open it at random, or flip to the theme that matches your week. Read the English, notice the Spanish beside it, then read the Spanish Note. If a line speaks to you, send it to someone, or write the Spanish phrase in your phone and use it once that day. That small habit, which I describe in {{link:sentence-mining-spanish|sentence mining}}, is how phrases move from the page into your own speech.

{{image:3}}

How it fits with my other books

Love, Slowly came after {{link:a-road-in-bloom|A Road in Bloom}}, my first bilingual book, which looks at growing up more broadly: family, money, friendship and peace. The third book, {{link:the-mind-lies|The Mind Lies}}, turns to psychology and why our minds trick us. All three share the same format, so you can move between them easily, and each one stands on its own.

A last word

If you read Love, Slowly, I hope it feels like a conversation with someone who has been there. And I hope that, somewhere between the pages, you find yourself saying something true in Spanish for the first time. If the book means something to you, I would love to hear about it on Goodreads.

faq.a: It is a bilingual book of 300 short truths about crushes, first dates, situationships, heartbreak, friendship, family and choosing yourself, with a Spanish Note on every page.

faq.q: Is Love, Slowly written in Spanish?
faq.a: It is written in English with real Spanish woven into every page, so you always understand the meaning while learning the Spanish.

faq.q: Do I have to read Love, Slowly in order?
faq.a: No. It is designed to be read in any order, one page a day.
The paperback has 304 pages. It was published in November 2026.
